headline: Finland's creative sector is split in mid-November 2026: Remedy and Marimekko reported growth, while smaller game studios keep closing, the EU's Digital Fairness Act initiative (11 November) threatens in-game purchase models, and textile innovation is still at demo scale but has the best-fitting open grants.

signals.title: Helsinki studio Playnest to cease operations; Rovio cuts about 20 jobs at Ruby Games
signals.detail: Neogames Weekly News 46/26 reports that Playnest (founded in late 2022 as Wonder Hive, 12 games published) is closing, and that Rovio is cutting around 20 jobs at Ruby Games in İzmir, Türkiye, with a smaller team keeping existing games running. No outcome of the RedLynx change negotiations is reported.

signals.title: New Finnish studio Silent But Deadly founded by Supercell and Remedy veterans; Supercell backs Anorak's $5M pre-seed
signals.detail: Silent But Deadly is backed by Sisu Game Ventures (amount not disclosed) and is developing a premium adventure game. Supercell took part in a $5M pre-seed round for Anorak (London and Chengdu, interactive generative-video formats and a creator platform), co-led by Play Ventures and Backed VC.

signals.title: EU Digital Fairness Act initiative published; Neogames calls it a threat to the game industry
signals.detail: According to Neogames, the Commission's initiative of 11 November 2026 would ban all in-game purchases by under-18s, treat each use of in-game currency as a separate purchase with a euro value shown, and ban loosely defined pay-to-win and pay-to-progress mechanics. This is Neogames' reading; the Commission text itself was not checked.

signals.title: EIC 2027 work programme adopted with €1.8 bn
signals.detail: The official EIC pages list Accelerator cut-offs on 20 January, 17 March, 1 September and 4 November 2027 (€428 m Open, €150 m Challenges) and an EIC Transition deadline of 14 September 2027 (€92 m, up to €2.5 m per project, single applicants allowed). Secondary guides add that Pathfinder Open becomes two-stage (stage 1 on 25 February 2027) and that Accelerator batches fall from six to four. The adoption date is taken from a news summary that could not be opened.

signals.title: Spinnova signs letter of intent with Outlast Technologies
signals.detail: Non-binding LOI to develop Spinnova fibre for insulation and temperature regulation. Spinnova's Woodspin demo factory is in trial runs, with larger-scale production targeted to restart during 2026, depending on trial results.

signals.title: Marimekko Q3: net sales up 3%, international sales up 16%, Finland down 9%
signals.detail: Q3 net sales were €52.1 m and comparable operating profit €13.0 m (25.0% margin). January–September net sales were €137.5 m with comparable operating profit of €23.4 m. Guidance is unchanged (growth on 2025's €189.6 m, margin about 16–19%), but Finnish sales are now expected to decline in 2026.

signals.title: Remedy Q3 revenue triples on CONTROL Resonant
signals.detail: Q3 revenue was €39.6 m (up 226%), EBIT €0.6 m (from a €16.4 m loss) and EBITDA €6.8 m. January–September revenue was €62.9 m with EBIT of -€2.3 m. CONTROL Resonant launched on 24 September and passed one million copies on 15 October. The 2026 outlook is unchanged.

signals.title: Aalto ranks third in Europe for spinout funding; Aalto Innovation unit replaces the Startup Center name
signals.detail: Aalto spinouts raised over €500 m in H1 2026 (mostly ICEYE) and about €2.6 bn since 2010. Eight research-based spinouts have launched in 2026 and the target is 20 a year. Twelve Research to Business teams will exhibit at Slush on 18–19 November 2026, and Aalto Innovation Week runs 16–20 November 2026. No design, textile, games or media spinouts are named.

signals.title: CREA news and media calls open
signals.detail: CREA calls on journalism partnerships, media literacy and media freedom open, with deadlines from 2027-01-20 to 2027-02-04.

signals.title: Ubisoft proposes closing RedLynx (Trials, Helsinki)
signals.detail: Part of a wider restructuring that includes about 70 roles in Singapore and about 100 in Germany. Subject to Finnish change negotiations; reports put the affected Finnish headcount at up to about 52.

signals.title: Horizon call on textile circularity opens (Textiles for the Future)
signals.detail: HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-08 is an Innovation Action call on advanced processing and manufacturing for textile circularity, due 2027-02-02.

signals.title: Q3 2026 gaming deal flow concentrated in AI and dev tools
signals.detail: Reported M&A of $2.4 bn over 45 deals and $1.6 bn+ over 106 funding rounds, mostly to AI and tools. Secondary source, not verified against Drake Star.

signals.title: Textile EPR fact sheet published; national transposition ahead
signals.detail: The revised Waste Framework Directive entered into force on 2025-10-16. Member states must transpose it by June 2027, and schemes are due by April 2028 (sources differ on the exact dates). Brands will pay eco-modulated fees based on durability and recyclability.

companies.name: Supercell
companies.what: Largest Finnish game company; second-largest corporate income taxpayer in Finland for 2025 (€216.4 m, group level) and an active investor in new studios and tools.

companies.name: Remedy Entertainment
companies.what: Listed AAA studio in Espoo; Q3 2026 revenue of €39.6 m after CONTROL Resonant sold over one million copies in three weeks.

companies.name: Rovio Entertainment (Sega)
companies.what: Angry Birds maker owned by Sega; cut about 20 jobs at its Ruby Games studio in Türkiye in November 2026.

companies.name: Metacore
companies.what: Mobile studio behind Merge Mansion; cut 159 jobs and closed its Germany and Sweden offices in 2026.

companies.name: Fingersoft
companies.what: Oulu studio behind Hill Climb Racing; Hill Climb Racing 2 marks its tenth anniversary in November 2026.

companies.name: Nitro Games
companies.what: Listed Kotka developer doing work-for-hire; signed a €1.1 m follow-on order in November 2026, bringing orders from that customer to about €5.2 m.

companies.name: Marimekko
companies.what: Listed design and lifestyle brand; January–September 2026 net sales of €137.5 m, with growth coming from international markets.

companies.name: Spinnova
companies.what: Listed wood-based textile fibre developer; Woodspin demo plant in trial runs, H1 2026 revenue of €286,000, and a non-binding letter of intent to buy Portuguese yarn spinner Tearfil.

companies.name: Infinited Fiber Company
companies.what: Textile-to-textile recycling (Infinna fibre) with brand backers including Inditex and Uniqlo; planning a commercial plant in Kemi and changing CEO.

companies.name: Woamy
companies.what: Aalto spin-out (Woamy Oy, registered 2022, Espoo) making bio-based cellulose foam materials.

companies.name: Lenzing
companies.what: Leading European producer of wood-based cellulosic fibres; industry partner in the Aalto-led MELANGE Horizon Europe project.

companies.name: Ubisoft
companies.what: Large European publisher under restructuring; proposed closing its Helsinki studio RedLynx (up to 52 positions) on 14 October 2026, outcome not yet confirmed.

aalto_links.what: Aalto Innovation: the new unit combining commercialisation services (replaces the Aalto Startup Center name); eight research-based spinouts in 2026, twelve Research to Business teams at Slush on 18–19 November 2026
MELANGE: Horizon Europe project on textile colouration led by Professor Maarit Salolainen, Department of Design (€4 m total, €1.5 m to Aalto; partners include Lenzing)
Ioncell: Aalto-developed process for textile fibres from wood or recycled textiles; Aalto is a co-founder of the company
Woamy: Aalto spin-out in bio-based foam materials
Aalto and VTT patent application on detecting elastane in textile samples with hyperspectral imaging (FI20236268A1, published 2025-05-16), relevant to textile sorting
Aalto patent application on separating cellulose and polyester from blended textile waste with a superbase ionic liquid (CN121065838A, published 2025-12-05)
Aalto game research and the GN! Event Week (9–15 November 2026, Annakaisa Kultima; Tim Schafer talk at Marsio), as listed by Neogames
Aalto cellulose and bio-based materials research: third most active institution worldwide in an OpenAlex search on textile recycling and cellulose fibre (174 papers); most cited paper linked
